params.prompt: A pre-existing condition is one for which the insured received medical advice, diagnosis or treatment, or had symptoms a prudent person would have treated, during a look-back period before coverage began, often six to twelve months. Older medical policies excluded such conditions for a waiting period. Federal law now forbids pre-existing condition exclusions in comprehensive medical coverage, so Marcus’s asthma is covered from day one. The exclusion still appears in disability income, long-term care, Medicare supplement, short-term and other excepted-benefit policies, each with its own look-back and exclusion period. Always check the type of coverage before applying the rule.

Policies exclude intentionally self-inflicted injuries, including injuries from a suicide attempt, because insurance covers accidental and unexpected loss. Mental health treatment for the underlying condition is a separate, covered matter under parity rules. Policies also exclude losses caused by war or an act of war, declared or undeclared, and often losses while serving in the armed forces, for which military coverage exists. If Rosa deliberately injures herself, her disability policy does not pay; if she is injured in a terrorist attack at home, most policies pay because that is not war between nations.

Elective cosmetic surgery, chosen to change appearance without a medical need, is excluded. Reconstructive surgery is different. Repairing a face after an accident, correcting a congenital defect in a child, or rebuilding a breast after a mastectomy restores function or appearance lost to injury or disease, and these are covered. Maryland specifically requires coverage of reconstructive breast surgery after a mastectomy, including surgery on the other breast for symmetry. The question to ask is why the procedure is being done. A medical cause moves the claim out of the exclusion.

Most individual and group health policies are nonoccupational. They exclude conditions covered by workers compensation, because that system is the primary payer for job-related injuries and illnesses. When Rosa is hurt on a job site, workers compensation pays her medical bills and partial wage replacement, and her health plan steps aside. Policies also exclude care furnished by government plans, such as treatment at a Veterans Affairs facility or under military coverage, and care for which the insured has no legal obligation to pay. The purpose is to avoid paying twice for the same loss.

Injuries sustained while committing or attempting a felony, or while engaged in an illegal occupation, are excluded. The uniform optional provision on illegal occupation, which Lesson seventeen covers, lets the insurer deny a loss arising from such activity. A person injured while burglarizing a warehouse cannot collect medical or disability benefits for those injuries. The exclusion requires participation in the crime; a bystander or victim injured during someone else’s felony is covered. Some policies similarly exclude losses while intoxicated or under the influence of unprescribed narcotics, again through an optional provision.

Exclusions are lists of causes, not lists of body parts. To decide a claim, identify the cause of the loss, then check it against the list. Asthma under a comprehensive medical plan: covered, because pre-existing exclusions are gone. A deliberate overdose: excluded as self-inflicted. A scar revision after a dog bite: covered as reconstructive. A fall at work: workers compensation, not the health plan. A broken leg during a robbery the insured committed: excluded. When two exclusions seem to apply, the one that actually caused the loss controls, and the burden of proving an exclusion generally falls on the insurer.

Theo drafts a postcard for A M G’s health clients. Maryland law and M I A rules require every advertisement to be truthful and not misleading in fact or by implication. The ad must identify the insurer, describe benefits accurately, and disclose limitations, exclusions and waiting periods with the same prominence as the benefits. It may not imply that a limited policy is comprehensive, exaggerate the ease of claims, or use testimonials that are not genuine. The insurer is responsible for every advertisement used on its behalf, including the producer’s own, which is why carriers require advance approval of producer materials.

Some claims are banned outright. An advertisement may not suggest that a policy is approved, endorsed or offered by a government agency, or use words such as Medicare or Social Security in a way that implies a government connection. It may not describe coverage as guaranteed issue when underwriting applies, or state that no medical questions will be asked when the application contains health questions. It may not misrepresent dividends, cash values or renewability. In Maryland, false advertising and misrepresentation are unfair trade practices that carry fines, restitution and license discipline, whether the author is the insurer or the producer.

If a member insurer becomes insolvent, the Maryland Life and Health Insurance Guaranty Corporation continues coverage and pays claims for Maryland residents, within limits. Coverage of health benefit plans, meaning major medical and basic hospital, medical and surgical coverage, is protected up to five hundred thousand dollars. Disability income and long-term care are each protected up to three hundred thousand dollars, life insurance death benefits up to three hundred thousand dollars, cash values up to one hundred thousand dollars and annuities up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars. Every authorized insurer and H M O must be a member and is assessed to fund the payments. Self-funded employer plans and nonadmitted insurers are not covered.

The corporation exists to protect policyholders after a failure, not to make a weak insurer look safe. Maryland law prohibits any person from using the existence of the guaranty corporation in the sale, solicitation or advertising of insurance. Theo may not say that a policy is backed by the state or that the client cannot lose because of the corporation. The insurer delivers a required summary notice about the corporation with the policy, and that notice itself states that the corporation may not be used in sales. Using the safety net as an inducement is grounds for discipline.

In Rosa’s kitchen, Theo presents a disability income policy. He identifies himself as a licensed producer and names the insurer. He explains the benefit amount, the elimination period and the benefit period before he mentions price. He states the exclusions, the pre-existing condition rule and whether the policy is noncancelable or guaranteed renewable. He compares policies only on accurate, complete terms and never disparages another insurer with false statements. He leaves an outline of coverage that summarizes benefits and limits. A fair presentation lets the buyer decide with the same facts the producer has.

Selling health insurance is persuasion built on accurate facts. Crossing the line means persuading with facts that are false, incomplete or implied. Omitting the elimination period, calling a hospital indemnity policy health insurance, hinting at government backing, or using the guaranty corporation to reassure a nervous buyer each crosses it. Maryland treats these as unfair trade practices with penalties that reach the producer personally. Later lessons on unfair trade practices and discipline return to these rules; this lesson gives you the standard: say what the policy does, say what it does not, and say who stands behind it truthfully.
